title: Fordham prints Vespucci's account of a voyage he presents as a new world
summary: Fordham prints Vespucci's letter claiming a mainland coast, with the voyage's identity still argued by scholars.
body: Fordham prints an account under Vespucci's name of a voyage along a coast he treats as a mainland, not islands off Asia. The letter is a European navigator's claim. Scholars dispute which voyage the letter describes. This card records the text Fordham prints, not a settled itinerary. The wording on the page includes: "example and instruction of the venerable monk friar of Saint Mark Fra Giorgio Antonio Vespucci: whose counsels and teaching would to God that I had followed: for as saith Petrarch, I should be another man than what I am. Howbeit soever I grieve not: because I have ever taken delight in worthy matters: and although these trifles of mine may not be". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
